root_cause.text: The `last_gc` timestamp was updated on every new connection addition instead of only after an actual garbage collection, allowing a high packet rate to continuously reset the GC timer and bypass cleanup, leading to infinite list growth.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `list->last_gc = (u32)jiffies;` from after `list->count++` (the new node insertion) to after the connection-pruning while loop, ensuring the timestamp is only updated when a GC cycle actually runs. The commit message explains that updating `last_gc` on every new connection lets a high packet rate bypass GC.
